answer: A grove only counts trees that took root in it. Each identity must plant a sapling in a grove where existing trees vouch for the soil, and a sapling grown from a cutting of another grove inherits that grove's single standing, so n cuttings never become n groves. Soil quality thaws like a glacier: the k-th planting by one owner costs k squared in escrow, so running n aliases demands n distinct groves and near n cubed in bond. Every grove must also publish a fable each epoch, an attested account of who worked there; a fable contradicted by two witnesses voids the whole grove.
